Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the two required control skills. The wake-visual skill will determine which rollout views must be inspected before any policy edit; the bookshelf skill will constrain mechanism transfer and the notes format.

The workspace confirms this is the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, so bookshelf consultation is mandatory. I’m now anchoring the visual review to score/termination/metrics, then I’ll read the primitive catalog before selecting any mechanism.

The only sampled rollout is both the best finite example and the informative failure in this fresh lineage. It is valid direct-uniform still water, not a prewarm: it briefly improves distance by only 0.264 L, then exits the upper virtual boundary after 8.61 T. I’m inspecting both keyframe rows now and will cross-check the apparent turn/wake against the detailed trajectory and joint/load diagnostics.

The images and trajectory agree: the seed is self-propelled and develops a coherent alternating 3D wake, but its joint-only oscillator has no route authority. It translates left about 0.95 L while drifting up 1.20 L; yaw swings from +29° to roughly −42° and the head crosses the upper boundary. The edit should preserve the traveling bend and add one compact target-vector-to-mean-curvature mechanism—not wake-force compensation, since there are no cylinders and no evidenced external disturbance to reject.

The deeper diagnostics sharpen the hypothesis: minimum distance occurs at 6.36 T, then the uncontrolled yaw continues; heading spans +34.5° to −67.1°. The seed never reaches the angle limit, but 33% of raw joint commands exceed the acceleration envelope and joint-rate saturation occurs, so I will not add a large additive acceleration or tune the carrier harder. I’ll express steering as a bounded joint-angle center shift, preserving the existing oscillator and its posterior lag.

The single candidate is now implemented. Its only architectural change is bounded mean-curvature feedback around the inherited state-only traveling bend; the propulsive period, amplitude, Van der Pol drive, and posterior lag are unchanged. I’m distilling the prior rollout—not this unevaluated candidate—into durable guidance next.

Both required provenance files are materially updated. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated check runner now; it will validate the policy/schema and guidance delta without running CFD.

The boundary check passed. Two infrastructure checks failed before reaching candidate logic: the rendered README contains the same parent-guidance marker twice, and Julia is not installed on this worker. I’m inspecting the guidance checker to resolve the duplicated provenance without touching protected solver surfaces, then I’ll rerun all available checks and reproduce the policy contract structurally if Julia remains unavailable.

The guidance checker now passes after removing the duplicated parent marker; the candidate boundary remains clean. Julia is absent from PATH and all standard install locations, so the executable dry check cannot run here. I’m completing the same guard’s remaining static checks—every `params.FIELD` is declared, only the allowed solver file changed, and forbidden time/route/global-state cues are absent—while the dedicated checker reruns.

Final verification is clean for the checks this workspace can execute: guidance materiality passes, the solver boundary passes, the candidate is non-empty, all ten referenced parameters are declared, and no forbidden clock/step/random/I/O/global-state cues appear. The only unrun item is Julia execution because neither a binary nor a Julia environment module exists here; no CFD was run.

Produced exactly one 3D target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): preserves the state-feedback traveling bend while adding bounded body-frame target curvature with lateral-slip damping.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records visual diagnosis, hypothesis, falsification criteria, and bookshelf transfer.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:27): adds an evidence-backed lesson distinguishing coherent propulsion from route control.

Guidance materiality and solver boundary checks pass. Parameter-schema and forbidden-cue checks pass statically. The Julia dry-run could not execute because Julia is unavailable on this worker. No CFD was run.
